subject: Post-demo scoping: inference validation tests & owners
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@optimed.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo scoping: inference validation tests & owners

Hi Samantha / team — thanks again for the demo time today. High-level recap and suggested next steps below so we all have alignment before the bake-off planning call on Friday.

Recap (from today's demo)
- OptiMed is primarily focused on: 1) real-time chart annotation (short prompts, 40–160 tokens), 2) bulk scoring for research workflows (batch jobs up to 32k tokens).
- They want predictable p95 latency under load for interactive UX and an acceptable cost per 1k tokens for nightly scoring runs.
- You ran a quick LLM output comparison vs CloudScale’s managed endpoint and saw parity on coherence, slight differences on instruction-following for long-context prompts.

Proposed validation tests (we should finalize owners/targets):
1) Interactive latency sweep (owner: Marcus)
   - Workload: 256-token average, 70/30 short/long mix, concurrency ramp to 50qps
   - Success: p95 end-to-end latency < 200ms (hosted), error rate < 0.5%
2) Batch throughput/cost (owner: Aisha)
   - Workload: 32k-token batches, 8 concurrent workers for nightly runs
   - Success: sustained throughput >= X tokens/sec and unit cost delta vs CloudScale <= 40%
3) Quality parity on instruction-following (owner: Neha + OptiMed SMEs)
   - Metric: semantic similarity + manual spot-checks on 120 prompts, with two failure buckets (hallucination, instruction-miss)
4) Failure & fallback behavior (owner: Marcus)
   - Test canary routing between models and region failovers; validate automatic fallback to quantized variant keeps p95 within 1.5x baseline

Attachments: I attached a first-pass test plan (20261120-opti-testplan.xlsx) and a small prompt set (opti-sample-prompts.json). Please review and flag any additions.

Immediate asks:
- Samantha: confirm the prompt set covers the priority flows (chart annotations + scoring).
- Rajiv / procurement: if procurement needs a separate timeline for SLA review / DocuSign, please share the procurement contact and timeline.
- Marcus / Aisha: can you confirm owners are OK and we can run a dry-run next Wed (Nov 25)?

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Re: Post-demo scoping: inference validation tests & owners

Thanks Neha — owners look good. A few clarifications from infra/ops perspective:

- For the interactive latency sweep I'd like to split into two tracks:
  A) P99 cold-start measurements (no KV cache warm)
  B) Steady-state p95 with KV cache warm (simulate repeated user sessions)
  Target p95 < 200ms will be for B; P99 cold-start we should expect higher (~400–600ms) and capture for transparency.

- For throughput/cost: we'll instrument token-level cost and per-request compute breakdown in the console so OptiMed can see clear unit economics. Aisha will wire the billing tags.

- I'll own the failure/fallback matrix. I'll also include a test for cross-region routing to simulate our fallback policy (us-west -> us-east) and measurement of added latency.

Next steps: Marcus to produce a short runbook (1–2 pages) describing the benchmark harness and data capture points by Tue EOD.

Marcus

I can take the batch throughput/cost instrumentation. Quick notes on what I'll include in the test plan: 
- Fixed dataset run (we'll use the opti-sample-prompts.json for quality + a separate sample_data.csv for throughput)
- Quantization profile testing: full-precision vs 8-bit vs dynamic quantization to measure cost/quality trade-offs
- Cache/cold-start separation so we can isolate savings from prefix/KV cache vs pure kernel perf
- Output: per-test CSV with tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, and a qualitative column for manual labelers to attach notes

I can have the initial harness and expected output CSV headers up by Tue morning (11/24) and run a dry-run Wed (11/25) if that still works.
